THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE V SRISHANANDA
ORAL ORDER
1. Heard Sri Mohan K.N., learned counsel for the revision petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for the State/respondent.
2. The Bailable Warrant is executed.
3. Revision petitioner voluntarily appears before the Court so also the de-facto complainant who has been identified by learned High Court Government Pleader.

4. Revision petitioner has suffered an order of conviction in C.C.No.966/2011 dated 11.06.2013 for the offences punishable under Section 498A and 506 of IPC which was confirmed in Crl.A.No.221/2013 dated 06.02.2016.
5.
A joint memo is filed on 12.12.2024 before this Court signed by the revision petitioner and de-facto complainant.
Learned HCGP has received copy of the joint memo and submits that the Court may take note of the subsequent development in the case and pass the suitable orders.

7. Taking note of the fact that there is subsequent development after the conviction order that the de-facto complainant along with her daughter is now staying with the revision petitioner and is leading a comfortable marital life, no useful purpose would be served by upholding the order of sentence of imprisonment at this distance of time.

8. However, the act that occurred earlier, which has been established by the prosecution before the trial Court and upheld by the First Appellate Court in recording the order of conviction for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 506 of IPC, cannot be effaced by the subsequent conduct of the accused.

9. Accordingly, following the dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Ramgopal v. State of Madhya Pradesh reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 834, matter NC: 2024:KHC:51124 can be disposed of by accepting the joint memo.

iii. If the fine amount as ordered by the learned Magistrate confirmed by the First Appellate Court is not paid, the revision petitioner shall pay the same on or before 31.12.2024.
